book.title: Humankind: A Hopeful History
book.summary: From the author of New York Times bestseller UTOPIA FOR REALISTS, a revolutionary argument that the innate goodness and cooperation of human beings has been the greatest factor in our success. If one basic principle has served as the bedrock of bestselling author Rutger Bregman's thinking, it is that every progressive idea -- whether it was the abolition of slavery, the advent of democracy, women's suffrage, or the ratification of marriage equality -- was once considered radical and dangerous by the mainstream opinion of its time. With Humankind, he brings that mentality to bear against one of our most entrenched ideas: namely, that human beings are by nature selfish and self-interested.

argument.statement: The innate goodness and cooperation of human beings, rather than selfishness, have been the greatest factors in human success and progressive change.

book.rationale: The book primarily argues for a hopeful view of human nature and its implications for societal progress, aligning it closely with themes of society and culture while also providing a historical perspective.
